q1_issues.issue: `(Symmetric Enemy)` makes the seeded `sym_rel` rule derive `(Enemy great good)`, but the aphorism asserts a directional relation (settling for good is what blocks great) and explicitly not its converse, so the symmetry tag manufactures a claim the text does not make.

q2_gaps: an asymmetric relational-noun copular predicate ("X is the enemy/rival/cause of Y") — the only open-class two-place relation licensed is the `Symmetric`-tagged mutual predicate, and the alternative `Inheritance`/`Member` + `Possession` route drops the directed link between the two arguments
notes: `Enemy` is open-class-licensed only through the `Symmetric`-tagged mutual-predicate route ("a relation the copula itself asserts to hold both ways"), so if the relation is directional here the head loses its licence along with the tag. Bare untyped `good` / `great` are acceptable as non-specific generic constants.
